okay, i've read it.

dropping the truth bomb now.

your experience section is the weakest part, and it should be the strongest. it's full of generic corporate speak.

"led the development", "enhanced user experience", "implemented best practices". this means nothing to a recruiter.

every single point needs to answer "so what?". you built a web app? so what? what did it *do*? how many people used it? did it make the company money? did it save time?

and i have to call this out. your "youtube clone" project says it's a "spotify clone".

that's a sloppy copy-paste error. an instant red flag for
Ok thanks any other advice

yeah, one more thing.

that long list of 'technical expertise'? it's just a keyword dump.

a hiring manager doesn't care that you *know* react. they care what you *built* with react.

instead of listing 'aws', say in your project description: 'deployed and scaled the app on aws, handling 10k users'.

show the skill in action. don't just list it. makes it real.
